Working document, not a publication. This is a private evidence compilation prepared for a commercial dispute and for the parties and advisers to that dispute. It is served with a no-index directive and is not intended for public circulation. Findings are drawn from message records and are stated as such; nothing here is a finding of any tribunal. Payment receipt images and financial identifiers have been withheld or masked in this hosted copy.

04

Direct contradictions on record

Vendor statement vs. vendor statement

These do not require any judgement about who was right. In each row the vendor's two positions cannot both be true, and both are timestamped in the vendor's own messages.

SubjectPosition APosition BConsequence
Pockets are technically impossible 15 Jul 18:04
"we dont do pockets in sublimation shorts bacause stitching affect the cloth and sublimated colour."		 16 Jul 10:32
"to make chain pocket in shorts it will cost 30 rs sir." Then 16 Jul 17:56: "WE ARE DOING ZIP AND POCKET SPECIAL CASE ONLY FOR THIS ORDER WITHOUT CHARGES."		 A stated physical limitation became a price, then became free. The technical justification was not accurate.
Production lock 13 Jul 16:42
"AFTER SENDING IT TO PRODUCTION NO CHANGES CAN BE DONE." Repeated 16 Jul 17:50: "THEN NO CHNAGE CAN BE DONE."		 Design changes were accepted on 22 Jul 12:54, 12:58 and 13:12, nine days after the first lock was asserted. The lock was used to compress approval time but was not real. Approval pressure was applied on a false constraint.
Colour code 29 Jul 17:23
"but sir we eaxctly matched the colour code believe me."		 No colour code, Pantone reference, hex value, CMYK breakdown or physical swatch appears anywhere in the four exported threads. The phrase "colour code" occurs exactly once in the entire record: in this defence. The vendor cannot evidence the standard it claims to have met. Colour was approved from a screen render only.
Ownership of production quality 29 Jul 17:30
"the color has been done perfectly according to the approved details."		 29 Jul 17:25
"sample hume jab recieve hoga hum tabhi share karenge sir" — conceding the goods sit with a third party the vendor does not control.		 The vendor certifies quality it also says it has not physically received. Both cannot hold.
Access to the goods 29 Jul 17:25
"but sir sample hume jab recieve hoga hum tabhi share karenge sir", followed at 17:26 by "hope aap yaha hote toh hum aapko show karte". Position: the vendor cannot show the product because it does not hold it.		 By that moment the vendor had already sent 21 photographs and one video of the same goods that same afternoon: 11:02 (1), 13:10:07–13:10:22 (10), 17:21:10–17:21:16 (9 plus video), 17:22:13 (1). The inability was asserted 3 minutes 35 seconds after the video was sent. Whatever access constraint existed did not prevent photography on demand once escalated. The stated constraint is contradicted by the vendor's own send timestamps within the same hour.
Delay attribution 13 Jul 16:08
Dispatch reset notice: design "abhi tak final nahi ki hain", so processing had not started.		 Client had confirmed final on 10 Jul 12:35 ("This is final now, these colors") and again 13 Jul 16:11 ("Final hai ye ji"). The vendor's own office had closed 11 Jul 18:30 with its own commitment: "will send it to printing on monday". Contested. The vendor's Monday-printing commitment was made unilaterally and was not met, before any client-side gap arose.

Why this matters more than it looks. A vendor that replies in a median of 78 seconds cannot claim it was unable to reply. The two longest gaps in the entire relationship, 145 hours and 77 hours, both open at the exact moment a photograph was promised. State that as a pattern in the record. Do not state it as proof of what they were thinking.

09

The design fee and the design labour

Rs.1,000 · 62 corrections · 4 working days

You raised this as a separate head of loss. It is a legitimate one, but it has to be pleaded accurately or it will be knocked out on a checkable number. Here is what the record actually supports.

PointWhat the record shows
What the Rs.1,000 was asked for 10 Jul 11:38 — "Pay 500, 1000 For Process Order To Design Team". It was demanded as a precondition to engaging the design team, not described as an order advance. Paid at 12:28, fifty minutes later.
Payment confirmation PhonePe transaction T2607101224477207683958, UTR 815263008536, paid to EIGHTX GLOBAL PRIVATE LIMITED (Vyapar…2119@hdfcbank), Rs.1,000, completed 10 July 2026, 12:24 PM — before the order group existed. Confirmed by screenshot; receipt on file.
How the vendor later treated it 14 Jul 16:17 — "680*20= 13600 RS ( 1000 DONE ) HALF = 5800 RS". The vendor set the Rs.1,000 off against the order total, computing 50% of 13,600 as 6,800 and invoicing the residual 5,800.
The correction you need to make Do not plead that you paid Rs.1,000 extra for design on top of Rs.13,600. On the arithmetic in their own message it was absorbed into the contract price. If you plead it as an extra, they produce that one line and your credibility on every other number in the complaint drops. Total remitted is Rs.6,800 against Rs.13,600. That is the figure to use.
The claim that does survive Consideration was taken specifically to engage a design team, and the design work was then substantially performed by RCC's own designers. That is a deficiency in the service actually contracted for, not an overcharge. It is a stronger argument and it costs you nothing to make it correctly.
Design labour supplied by RCC 62 design-direction and correction messages from the two RCC designers between 11 Jul 17:24 and 16 Jul 17:12, across four working days (11, 13, 15 and 16 July). This is measured from the transcript, not estimated.
Rework caused by vendor-side design error Logo colour and sizing corrections (11 Jul 17:28, 17:29, 18:19). Drop shadow and stroke iterations (11 Jul 17:27, 17:42, 13 Jul 13:20, 13:21). Approved font substituted without approval and caught by RCC (15 Jul 18:22). Letter spacing, centering and font-size inconsistencies raised repeatedly (16 Jul 16:43, 16:52, 16:55, 17:02, 17:04, 17:07), including an offer by RCC to walk the vendor through its own software settings (13 Jul 13:33).
How to quantify it Do not invent an hourly rate. Put it as: design service paid for and not delivered, plus 62 documented corrections over four working days by two RCC personnel. If you want a number, use your designers' actual billed or notional day rate and show the working. A forum will accept a reasoned figure and will discount an asserted one.
